text:
tara: Quick recap from the GPTQ bakeoff across Llama / Mistral / Qwen. TL;DR: GPTQ (per-channel, omp-k=64) was the best accuracy/cost tradeoff for the Llama family; AWQ surprisingly competitive on Mistral for short-context generation; INT8 gave best memory footprint but showed 0.8-1.5% BLEU/EM delta on long-context QA for Llama-7B. FP8 results are noisy across families. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/gptq-bakeoff-1759/ (csv + profiles + raw logs). Please read the small summary below and flag anything you want deeper.
kevin: nice. can you paste the top-line table here? quick numbers help decisions.
tara: sure, quick table (accuracy delta = quantized - fp32, pos is better):
```
model          quant   acc_delta  latency_delta  mem_savings
llama-7b       gptq    -0.9%      +5ms           2.1x
llama-13b      gptq    -1.3%      +8ms           2.0x
mistral-7b     awq     -0.4%      +12ms          2.3x
qwen-7b        int8    -1.5%      -2ms           2.8x
```
(note: latency_delta = quantized - fp32 on our infra; mem_savings = fp32_mem / quant_mem)
sam_m: can you also share throughput numbers for the deployment profiles? i.e. tokens/sec at target batch sizes.
tara: short numbers from perf-run-1 (p100-ish cluster):
- Llama-7B GPTQ: 1.2k tok/s @ batch=8, peak mem ~4.2GB
- Mistral-7B AWQ: 980 tok/s @ batch=8, peak mem ~3.8GB
- Qwen-7B INT8: 1.5k tok/s @ batch=16, peak mem ~3.1GB
So INT8 is great for raw throughput but had the worst accuracy regression on long-context QA.
jonathan: what thresholds are we using to decide "reject" vs "allow with guardrails"? we need concrete rollback criteria for Dedicated customers.
tara: suggested gates from the bakeoff:
- accuracy regressions >1.0% absolute on our aggregated QA/eval set => block rollout unless retrain/adjust quant config.
- regressions between 0.3% and 1.0% => canary-only + monitored quality alerts tied to prompt-set holdouts.
- latency increase >15% => fail SLA for latency-sensitive tiers (Dedicated/Enterprise) -> require alternative (int8/fp32) route.
We also add per-route eval hooks and automatic fallback to fp32 model variant for top-n worst queries.
eval-bot: auto-eval summary: Llama-7B (gptq-perchannel) => avg EM -0.85%, Mistral-7B (awq) => avg EM -0.42%, Qwen-7B (int8) => avg EM -1.47%. All evals run across 12 held-out prompt suites (translation / long-form QA / summarization / code).
kevin: good. one follow-up: AWQ for Mistral — is it stable for >2048 tokens? we saw some KV-cache noise earlier.
tara: AWQ had slight drift after 2k tokens in one seed (repro 0.2% on long-code tasks). We recommend capping AWQ models to 2048 until we patch the runtime kv-cache handling (ticket ENG-RUN-2043).
infra-bot: deploy plan template created: canary=5% traffic for 48h -> pct-based roll with metrics: 99th latency, avg token cost, eval-accuracy delta. See /infra/deploy-templates/gptq-canary-compact.
sam_m: i'll spin up a Mistral AWQ canary in dedicated pool tomorrow AM. assigning myself to add a prompt-holdout monitor.
jonathan: please also wire the rollback policy to the Console so product/security teams can approve forced rollbacks.
tara: noted. action items: sam_m -> canary + monitor; kevin -> dig into the 2k-token AWQ kv drift; infra -> add rollout template to Dedicated fleet (infra-bot assigned). i'll upload the full CSV and per-run profiles to the s3 link and open a short PR with the eval harness and config snippets.
kevin: :thumbsup: will look at kv-cache repro today.
sam_m: :eyes: scheduling canary for 2026-03-19 09:00 PT.
tara: thanks all — if no objections i'll close this thread end of day and open per-model issues for follow-ups.
eval-bot: uploaded run artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/gptq-bakeoff-1759/summary.csv (sha256: b3f2...)
infra-bot: canary template updated in infra repo -> PR #4126.
